title: Linkages and Consciousness
path: RS2-1: The inanimate, physics, chemistry, astronomy

posts.content:
When reviewing some of Nick Thomas' work on counterspace, I again ran across his idea of "linkage points" between space and counterspace. These points anchor specific locations in one system to the other, and thus give an orientation to motion that would otherwise not have any direct representation in the conventional reference system. We see these as geometric structures, most notably in living systems, such as helices, leaf patterns, ovals, corkscrews and anything non-linear.

Larson's "life unit" may well represent this type of linkage point between the material and cosmic sectors, about which cosmic motion can then influence the behavior of the biological representation.

One of the things that has been consistent in the RS2 re-evaluation, is that the same patterns repeat over and over, and there do not appear to be any exceptions. Only the scale changes, which makes sense in a system rooted in scalar motion. If this consistency holds true, then there must be linkage points in all aspects, not just the life unit. There will be inanimate linkage points, ethical ones (control units) and linkages between regions and frames.

If we go right to the very base of the system in RS2 in the projective layer, we have the "ratio". (This is basically a more generic term than "motion", which Larson uses to convey the same idea.) I often wondered why the projective stratum had the invariant of the cross-ratio, rather than just the "ratio", which, all other things being equal, doesn't change magnitude and is therefore invariant.

Thomas' linkage points gave me the reason. The cross-ratio is the first manifestation of this linkage concept we find in the RS2 system. And this led to some ideas on exactly what this "linkage" is.

Take, for example, a ratio of 5/7. How does one know that the magnitudes ARE 5 and 7? Because of a thing called consciousness, which creates a linkage between a zero reference--the point of consciousness that does the "perceiving"--and the item under observation, in this case, the ratio of 5/7. Since everything in this stratum is based on the ratio, the idea of a "zero" for a ratio isn't actually a zero, but a zero displacement from UNITY, 1/1. Thus, with another ratio--our consciousness--fixed at 1/1, we can therefore measure the CROSS-RATIO of 1/1:5/7 and have an accurate measurement of 5 and 7.

This is the reason for the cross-ratio; it is a linkage between ratios where one can define the other. And once defined, the magnitudes can be measured. The pure ratio, alone with no basis of measurement, cannot have a defined magnitude and is therefore variant in the projective layer.

The "linkage point" is the creation of a reference for which things can be measured by consciousness. Indeed, set set of linkages between the various frames, sectors, and regions may actually constitute what we call "consciousness", because it literally determines how we "see" things, in many senses of the word.

There are some interesting consequences to this idea. "Things" occur all over the Universe, whether we are here to observe them or not. "Reality" is basically the consensus of observation AND communcation--not just the objects, themselves, but the connections between them. "Local" and "non-Local" existence, if you prefer. All these "things" in the Universe have linkage points within them, defining some basic relationships and structure. For example, whether the vibration of a photon moves with the progression, producing heat, or orthogonal to it, producing light. The behavior is determined by that linkage of orientation. But it also occurs outside the observation of our consciousness, and since "linkage" is "consciousness", then the conclusion is that the "things" of the Universe are "conscious," unto themselves, and our interaction with them is one consciousness communicating with another -- not a conscious observer of a non-conscious "thing."

I avoided the use of the term "unconscious", because it appears that many of these linkage points are what would be termed "unconscious connections" between realms, insomuch as they are, like the linkage of the cross-ratio, archetypal in the sense that they are always present within the structure, and most likely invariant.

I am putting out these ideas primarily for consideration at this time. The concept makes a lot of sense to me internally, but it is very difficult to express, since I cannot find reasonable analogies or processes to explain it, particularly since the background material I have built it upon is not well known. But, at least for me, it may turn out to be the Rosetta Stone that allows me to pull together the other concepts in RS2 into a true model of a simple Universe, based on a few rules with no exceptions. And that should open the door to some interesting discoveries.

posts.content:
This may be slightly OT, but this post brought to mind the "protein folding problem". Stated somewhat simply, it goes like this:

Proteins are long chains of amino acids that fold up into various shapes depending on the chemistry of the types of amino acids involved. But this isn't the whole story. It turns out that it's impossible to predict the shape of the folded protein based on the chemistry of the amino acids alone, and not because the final shape is purely random, but precisely because it isn't random. Among all the possibilities of a given amino acid chain, there can be multiple minimum energy states, yet not only will the chain always fold into a specific shape every time, it will fold up into the same shape every time. It does not waffle between the multiple minimum possibilities, sometimes taking shape A, and at other times shape B.

You would think that if we took a gob of denatured chains of amino acids and threw them into an ideal broth for folding, we would find proteins reflecting all the possible minimum configurations; as it's purely random, we may find 30% take state A, 20% state B, and 50% state C. Instead, we always find, say, state A. Now, state A may be slightly "more" minimum, but it will be hard to verify as none of the other state comes into existence! And neither does the protein take various shapes as it "whittles" it's way toward a minimum energy state. It's been calculated that due to the enormous possible configurations for any chain of amino acids, this could take between 10^50 to 10^77 years. In fact, we know some can fold in a matter of minutes or seconds, even on the scale of microseconds. It seems the protein follows a pre-determined path toward its conformation rather than random one.

It's difficult for me to conceive, but it always seemed to me the answer to this problem lies in cosmic sector influences, as if the final shape of the protein is constrained, like a "groove" that is difficult to escape from. Can you see, offhand, if or how linkages may play into this?

danmc wrote:
It's difficult for me to conceive, but it always seemed to me the answer to this problem lies in cosmic sector influences, as if the final shape of the protein is constrained, like a "groove" that is difficult to escape from. Can you see, offhand, if or how linkages may play into this?
Have you looked at denaturation of proteins, the process of unfolding a protein? One of the most notable features is that most of the time, denaturation is irreversible, which means that the protein has reverted to inanimate status. The component amino acids may still be intact and viable, but the life that was the protein is gone.

Based on a cursory examination, I would conclude that the folding of a protein is it being "born" as a life unit of a protein (according to Larson). And by my recent interpretation of "linkage", it occurs when that linkage point is created between the component amino acids -- not the chemical orientation of amino acids.

Denaturation is when a protein dies, and the linkage is broken.

As to why the protein always folds into the same shape; well, I refer back to Steiner's 3rd world, the world of archetypal forms--where the concept of "empty" and "full" are flipped around. It is not limited just to proteins... why does an acorn always look like an acorn? Probability should indicate quite a variation, given the number of components that go into its DNA structure.

I started to touch on this in the first post, but I have found that there are two basic linkage types, unconscious links, which seem to form these "molds" to which shapes conform, and conscious links, which are determined by valuing systems, like the Memes discussed on the Phi-Core forums.

All of this comes back to a concept introduced back in the 1970's called a "holon", based on the Greek word "holos" meaning "wholly contained". In computer programming, a holon is like a class, with its super-class and sub-classes ... basically, templates of object and function which can be "real-ized" thru instances of the class.

The same thing is occuring here, in a general, physical sense where motion is the objective part of the class, and linkage is the functional part. Together, they define a shape and behavior "template" which we tend to refer to as an archetype.

Chemical interactions, such as those described in folding a protein, are not linkages... they are objects orienting themselves to achieve minimum distortion (kind of like we all do in our lives!) So when they base an analysis solely on the objective part of the holon (analogous to just using the variables, and not the functions in the instance of a "class"), they are missing half the picture.

The same problem will occur if you examine the linkages only (use the functions, but ignore the variables in the class). It is analogous to trying to work only with space, and ignore "time", as legacy physicists do.

There are other features of the object-oriented model of classes in computers that give us more to think about (as I've said, the same interactions repeat over and over...) One of them is "extending" a class, which takes a generic class (like a shopping cart program) and tailors it to a specific need (a specific store). Holons can also be extended, so the generic holon that defines the base objects (aminos) and functions (fold orientation) of a protein can be customized for specific proteins, producing a range of similar, but unique, proteins. BUT... their structure, composition and behavior cannot wander outside the limits of the defining holon, so it remains constrained (in the "groove", as you mentioned).

Another feature of classes is that they can contain any number of "instances", so there will be many, many instances of the same series of proteins, defined by the base holon and its extensions.

As to what creates "motion" or "linkage" to being with... that will probably remain a mystery. But once the process is started, just as you can add motion to other motions, to produce compound, aggregate or assocaited motions, the SAME principle will apply to linkages. Links can add to other links, to produce compound, aggregate or associated links, which we interpret as varying degrees of consciousness, and the rational and irrational valuing systems.

This is the big piece that was missing in RS2. We were handling the interaction of motions correctly, but did not handle its compliment--the interaction of linkage, itself. By adding this in, the RS2 concepts will be updated to include ideas such as "archetypal particles", as templates for the combination of motion and linkage (which we've already been doing, unconsciously, with Nehru's concept of bi-rotation, which is a "linkage" between two electrons -- kind of a "cross-ratio of electrons").

It should be interesting, particularly since it now lends itself so well to computer models and simulation. Class structures are the archetypal templates, instances simulate the actual particles with their specific speeds and energies.

posts.content:
The investigation of linkages has revealed (so far) that there are three different types of linkages between space and time, based on the concept of the "opposites":
  1. Multiplicative Inverse -- the standard reciprocal relationships used by Larson, commonly referred to as "division".
  2. Additive Inverse -- things of opposite polarity that can cancel each other out, commonly referred to as "subtraction".
  3. Conjugate -- similar to the multiplicative inverse, more commonly referred to as reflective symmetry. (Nehru identified in another post that the cosmic sector is the conjugate of the material, not its inverse.)
What these linkage point do, is to create a dichotomy or polarity between what would otherwise be identical "concepts" (for lack of a better word). They are the separators, the dividers, the differentiators... those things that make "One" into "Two". Pythagoreas referred to this is "will" acting upon the monad to produce the dyad, and from the investigation so far, it appears he was right.

The basic relationship we first encounter in RS2 is that of the ratio, for you must have ratio before you can have cross-ratio. From the original Unity, that unit motion we know as the speed of light in a vacuum, something happens. The philosophical concept of that something is "free will" acting upon the original Unity, producing dichotomy -- a balance of opposites. Thus, 1 becomes 1/2 x 2/1, and the idea of the "ratio" is created. In this particular case, since there is not yet a concept of "dimension", there is no difference between a multiplicative inverse and a conjugate... they are identical.

This ratio can also be viewed either as an inverse OR a polarity, the polarity being +1 and -1, respectively. This gives us some information into the linkage known as the polarity--polarity is a measurement of displacement, not one of ratio, speed or motion.

Put mathematically: 1 = 2/1 x 1/2; the displacements being 0 = (1-2) + (2-1). (The displacement being the difference between denominator and numerator (time and space) as discussed in another post).

Linkages then become different ways to look at the separation of some type of structure. At the very base level, that structure simply being a magnitude (a number). And being a "way to look at something" brings it right into the field of Projective Geometry.

When a linkage point creates a dichotomy, TWO perspectives are established. Just as the ratio of 3/4 can be also be viewed as 4/3, if you are standing on your head. The perspective is a matter of interpretation of an observer, not an actual truth of the Universe.

The ratio only has a self-perspective. The only reference it has is the "opposite point of view". But, when two ratios also become linked, the concept of a "direction" is formed, in which one ratio can now be viewed in multiple perspectives, including from outside of itself. This is where Larson's concept of scalar motion comes into play, and actually requires THREE linkage points -- one each creating the dichotomy of ratio, and one of the dichotomy of the dichotomy.

When we get to the point of multiple, interacting dimensions, the difference between the inverse and conjugate manifests itself. Take, for example, the concept of "acceleration", which is speed per unit of time, s/t * 1/t = s/t2:

Inverse acceleration is then: t2/s (inverse dimensional relations)

Conjugate acceleration is then: t/s2 (same dimensional relations)

This indicates that the conjugate type of linkage makes its appearance somewhere between the affine and metric strata of projective geometry. This is rather confusing, because one would not think that a "linkage" is an actual, physical event within a specific geometric stratum, since a "linkage" is technically just an "assumption" created by consciousness in order to perceive something.

From this, I am inferring that there is something more substantial to the devices we use to transform perspective -- that the transform, itself, is a type of "motion", as Larson would put it--or better yet, the inverse concept to the concept of "motion".

I have yet to locate ANY information at all on prior research along this line of thinking, so I am at a total loss of terminology to describe what I mean. If anyone is aware of research concerning the perceptual transformation that IS consciousness, I'd like to know about it.

In essence, we have some basic concept called "magnitude" that sits at the root of all things. Magnitudes are related thru linkage, producing ratio, cross-ratio and all the manifestations of motion Larson and RS2 describe. Linkage = 1/magnitude, for lack of a better expression.

[/]

Was chatting with Dan tonight about linkages and how to define them. Came up with a fairly accurate analogy...

If one were to accept that "Free Will" is the first distortion from Unity (a type of "displacement"), then in a polarized system that "free will" would have two manifestations, a "local" form and a "non-local" form, which we term "motion" and "linkage", respectively.

This is more apparent in the study of psychology, where expression takes the form of symbols (motion, aka "particles") and motifs (linkage, "waves"). Together, motion and linkage form a type of particle-wave duality.

From this, we can infer that a "linkage", as proposed by Nick Thomas in his work on Counterspace, is an actual "thing" as manifest as Larson's "motions". Question is... what kind of "thing" is a linkage?

The basic property of a link is that it connects a material and cosmic structure together. The logical conclusion is therefore that the link cannot exist in either space nor time, but must be part of another "sector", to use Larson's word. This sector would be the third, "ethical" sector of Larson, or the realm that sits in conjugate with the physical sectors (material and cosmic), which we could refer to as a "non-physical" or "meta-physical" sector.

Thus, the physical Universe is composed of one component, motion, and the metaphysical Universe is composed of one component, linkage -- local and non-local expressions of the concept of "free will", which, for lack of a better term, being the underlying consciousness that forms and connects everything.

Here's another thought on linkages, inspired by Gopi's comment on connections and evolution:

We know from Larson's work that only the net magnitude of motion can be transmitted across the unit boundary. Directional information is lost in the crossing. For example, the coordinate time structure inside the time region is perceived only as a single magnitude, the atomic number. All the temporal orientation is lost.

Linkages, being the inverse of "motion", should therefore have reciprocal properties to motion. As we have seen with space and counterspace, where "out" becomes "in" and "bounded" becomes "unbounded", the linkage should therefore have the property of transmitting direction across the unit boundary, and losing all "magnitude" information.

So we have found yet another type of geometric "reciprocal relationship":

Motion: transmits magnitude, blocks direction = "local" structure.

Linkage: transmits direction, blocks magnitude = "non-local" structure.

Starts to make a lot of sense when you think about how non-locality works. Its effect is "infinite"--no loss of magnitude, because "magnitude" is not a transmitted property of linkage. And only the orientation is affected.

The books Dan sent me on counterspace included works on the "plant" being a linkage between the material and cosmic sectors, namely Larson's "life unit." The basic shapes of plant structures, seeds, flowers, leaf patterns and branches can be derived using the intersection of rectangular and polar geometries -- the geometric conjugates between the material and cosmic sectors.

For the system to work, it required "linkages" to map directional information between the two geometries, producing a recursive heirarchy of structure. The authors would just pick points, and demonstrate how the patterns would be extracted.

Now we see that the linkages, which transmit direction only, are therefore scale variant, since there is no "magnitude"--the same patterns can be used at any scale, and would easily produce recursive heirarchies--scaled versions of the same pattern, like a Mandelbrot set.

It will take me a while to work out the projective invariants of the non-local (polar) strata, but a quick look at the Euclidean version:

Euclidean (local): scale invariant, fixed at unity; length and direction variant.

Polar Euclidean (non-local): scale variant; length and direction invariant.

Thus, the non-local form of linkage would appear locally as a series of fixed "patterns", to which life units (being a connection between the local and non-local) would conform to, more commonly known as "archetypal" patterns--molds or templates for manifestation.

This is probably the basis of the "3rd world" that Anthroposophy and I believe Theosophy speaks of, that contains the "molds" to form the shapes we see, here in the 1st world.

This also brings up an interesting philosophical point. If non-locality is, indeed, infinite, then the life patterns we see here on Earth will be available EVERYWHERE in the Universe, and any planet with similar conditions where life can form, will produce the SAME living structures we see here on Earth, slightly adjusted for differences in the environment.

So any Earth-type planet should have Earth-type archetypal life: oak trees, elephants, whales... and even humans. Interesting thought, isn't it?

Gopi wrote:

Superb observation, Gopi! I believe you hit that right on the mark. Non-local expression will be limited to the Logos, not infinity.

Using "as above, so below" logic, sub-logoi should inherit all the archetypes of the parent logos, which then can then "customize", pass on "as-is", or create an entirely new archetype unique to that logos. So, some questions arise:

1) How is a "logos" defined; what is its extent; what delimits it.

2) Is there any way to tell what archetypes were inherited from parent logoi, versus a local creation?

3) Are the "laws of physics" actually mutable, since they are archetypal patterns of the expression of the free will of the parent logos? (As a sub-logos, yourself, you should be able to modify them -- "magick", perhaps?)

In the Ra Material, it was said that we were part of a "free will" logos, and that there were non-free-will logoi out there. Without free will, things still manifest but lack "consciousness" as a valuing system. In other words, they respond to "pre-destination" only. Pre-destination is basically being carried by something to where you are needed to be, analogous to a photon being carried by the progression of the natural reference system.

So, is pre-destination then the "outward" linkage of the natural reference system, similar to the outward motion that moves objects apart from each other? Since linkage is the reciprocal of motion, then what is "outward linkage" non-locally would be "inward linkage", locally -- massive formation of connections between motions: compound motions, atoms, molecules, aggregates, etc.

Left to pre-destination, as the complexity of motion increases, the probability of linkage would decrease. Thus, in a non-free-will environment, the more complex life becomes, the fewer of those life forms would be around. We actually observe this in the taxonomy of life--compare the number of microbes to the number of trees to the number of people.

Philosophers have long recognized a relationship between free will and predestination. Psychologists refer to it as the "conscious" and "unconscious" aspects of personality. With reference to the Reciprocal System, to me it looks like a "direction reversal", where the progression of the natural reference system, as non-local linkage, is the default, and "free will" is "inward motion" that defies pre-destination.
